newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian bonds end weaker, yield curve steepens.
newsitem.headline: Canadian bonds end weaker, yield curve steepens.

text.p: Canadian bonds closed weaker on Tuesday with the yield curve steepening slightly, as the market took much of its direction from weakness in U.S. treasuries, analysts said.

"It seems to be the weakness in the U.S. Treasury market," said Dawn Desjardins, a fixed-income analyst with J.P. Morgan Canada. "As well I think that people are unwinding some curve- flattening trades."
Canada's 30-year benchmark bond rose C$0.78 to C$118.05 to yield 6.605 percent.
The U.S. 30-year bond fell 14/32 to yield 6.68 percent. The negative spread between the bonds widened to eight basis points from seven basis points at Monday's close.
Canadian bonds, which opened stronger, turned lower late in the session with U.S. treasuries after the release of a stronger than expected Redbook report in the United States.

Investors in both markets are now seen focusing on two key U.S. economic reports out on Wednesday. The U.S. retail sales report and producer price index for July are seen as important indicators of both growth and inflation presssures.
In money market trade, this afternoon's auction of C$4.3 billion in Government of Canada T-bills was well bid.

But dealers said the short-end of the yield curve is distorted by a squeeze which has taken place in the one-year cash T-bill. The one-year cash bill is trading with a yield of 3.95 percent, compared with a 4.21 percent yield for the one-year when-issued contract.
"Someone has basically bought them all as WI's," said one T-bill trader with a bank-owned brokerage. "Today as people scrambled to try to cover they just became ridiculous."
In other prices, Canada's 10-year benchmark bond fell C$0.38 to C$108.50 to yield 6.083 percent. The U.S. 10-year bond fell 8/32 to yield 6.40 percent.
The negative spread between the bonds narrowed to 32 basis points from 33 basis points at Monday's close.
The 10-year Canadian government bond futures contract trading on the Montreal Exchange closed down 0.20 to 119.08 with 4558 contracts traded, up from 4112 yesterday.
